reviews.title: Same paid features removed again with no permanent fix
reviews.text:
I bought PDF Converter separately in 2018 for $4.99, entitling me to permanent conversion access under the terms sold at the time. This is the second time Readdle has revoked that access, first in 2025, now again in June 2026, both times forcing me to argue with support and provide old receipts just to get back something I already paid for.

Their own published FAQ for PDF Expert 7 states clearly that PDF Converter purchasers retain conversion access. Support initially denied this, incorrectly claiming I only had access due to a subscription. After I pushed back with documentation, they eventually issued a one-year redemption code, but refused to guarantee anything beyond that. I now have to fight for this same access annually with no permanent resolution in sight.

Readdle has since scrapped one-time purchases entirely in favor of subscriptions, which makes it painfully clear how they now view anyone who bought in before that shift: an inconvenience to be quietly phased out. I’ve used this app for nearly eight years and would rather not leave, but I can no longer recommend it in good conscience until this is resolved permanently.

You’re better off going to ilovepdf.com which provides all of the same editing and conversion features for free that Readdle has locked their legacy customers out with a paid subscription paywall time and time again.

Except that everyone used to sell software for a fixed price and now everyone (almost) has gone to a subscription model. Not going to happen for me. I live on a fixed income and can’t afford to pay monthly or yearly for every app I own.

I gave up on Adobe for this very reason. Plus their whole suite of software is an unholy mess: good luck uninstalling apps you don’t want.

Lastly, I’m a normal guy with an iPhone, an iPad Pro, and a MacBook Pro. I might be mistaken but does one license not cover all my devices (using the same Apple ID)? I want to support Readdle and Ukraine but I can’t print money. I’m going to have to look at less expensive options. Sorry.

I have, today, received the following email: "...To check why the convert and merge features are no longer available on your device, could you please send us a screenshot of your PDF Expert purchase. If you bought it through the App Store, please share a screenshot of the receipt or your Apple purchase history showing PDF Expert (the lifetime/grandfathered purchase)..."   

After receiving much backlash, PDF agreed years ago to honor the paid features of the original one-time fee version through an announcement made on their website. 

To be clear, the “lifetime/grandfathered purchase” would have been only for features available before subscription conversion and I was fine with that.   

When I attempt to restore purchase from their app, I am able to execute and receive notice of "a successful restore of my purchase" but original purchased features have now been stripped. If there was, in fact, no one-time purchase or paid subscription a notice to that effect would be stated.

reviews.title: Features constantly asking to upgrade
reviews.text:
I’ve been a paying user of Readdle’s iOS PDF tools for a while, and the recent UI changes have made the experience noticeably worse.

The main issues:

* A prominent AI button has been added to the centre of the UI with no option to remove or disable it
* PDF tools now mix core paid features with subscription-only features, making it unclear what is actually included
* Upgrade prompts now appear frequently and interrupt normal workflow
* There’s no toggle to turn off these promotional elements

The result is that the app feels increasingly designed around upselling rather than supporting the workflow I originally paid for.

What makes this more frustrating is that the Mac version doesn’t currently have the same level of UI intrusion, so it feels inconsistent across platforms.

As someone who already paid for the app, I don’t want extra features I didn’t ask for getting in the way of basic functionality. If subscription features are being added, they should be clearly separated, not blended into the core interface.

At minimum, there should be a simple toggle to disable AI buttons and promotional UI elements for users who prefer a clean, paid-only experience.

Imagine Readdle a company wanting donations for the War actively committing UI invasion on the app. Ironic.

reviews.title: Used it for years...until 2025
reviews.text:
Why I stopped using this app: PDF Expert can no longer easily sync PDFs across devices via third-party cloud service (iCloud, Dropbox, etc.).

I have to manually download the PDF to PDF Expert, make my changes, and then manually upload the file to again after I am done editing the PDF — it’s like stepping back at least a decade.

It's way easier in Apple’s Preview (or — shudder — Adobe Acrobat). I just open the PDF and make my changes. Then the PDF is *automatically* uploaded to the cloud where my other devices quickly see the changed file — no manual downloading and uploading. That default behavior saves loads of time and storage space — and, with Apple, money (because Preview is free).

Were it not for this massive cloud syncing disadvantage (and Readdle’s increasing reliance on subscription and even removing features people had in prior paid versions), my review would be as follows:

I've used the app (or its prior versions) for years. And I regularly try other PDF apps. This app always outperforms the competition. No other PDF app comes close. 

And now that PDF Expert has a Mac/OSX counterpart, it's beginning to look like an ideal cross-platform solution. (Alas, PDF Expert for Mac/OSX isn't yet best in class, like its iOS counterpart, so that ideal has yet to be actualized).
